notes: Birthday probabilities use the standard approximation 1 - exp(-n(n-1) / 2^(bits+1)).
Checksum analysis assumes the 32-bit double-SHA-256 checksum is uniform over random corruptions; the drill measured 12/12 malformed inputs rejected, including a bad checksum.
The 2^160 AccountID space is what makes accidental collision negligible; the realistic confusion risks are encoding-level (same key, different format) not hash collisions.
